Gates I ran on `82a7711b9`: `go build ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./cmd/...`, `mise run lint` (0 issues), `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/ ./cmd/entire/cli/settings/` (105s), and `go test -tags=integration -run TestEnableCheckpointPushRemote`. All pass. The integration tests are the strongest part of this branch — real per-backend routing, the disabled-push case, project-settings preservation, and "fails before any write" are all covered, and the unit tests assert URL redaction in the picker labels, which is easy to forget.

Four findings filed separately. Below are the things I deliberately did not file as findings, because they are calls for you rather than defects.

**The report now fires on every `entire enable`, after `Ready.`** In a plain single-remote repo the command ends with three extra lines, and in a repo with no remotes at all with two:

```
Ready.
Keeping checkpoint destination: origin (automatic)
No checkpoint destination settings changed.
Checkpoints will be uploaded when you push to origin.
```

Your README says the command "confirms the effective destination", so confirming is intended — but text continuing past the closing `Ready.` line reads like the command was not finished, and `No checkpoint destination settings changed.` announces the absence of a change nobody asked for (on a first-time enable there was nothing to change). Worth considering scoping the report to invocations that actually touched the destination, or to repos where it is ambiguous, which is what the note it replaced did.

**The picker re-asks on every bare `enable` in a multi-remote repo.** "Keep current destination" writes nothing, so the conditions are unchanged next time. That follows from the description ("appears when multiple remotes exist and no explicit choice is set"), so it is the design rather than a bug — but it does mean bare `entire enable` stops being the lightweight re-enable path the comment at setup.go:1173 describes, with no way to answer "stop asking" short of pinning a remote.

**Follow-up issue, not for this PR: #2360.** `validateCheckpointPushRemote` is correct and the description explicitly scopes it in, but it is a fourth definition of "usable remote" living in `cli`, so election and `status` still accept a pushurl-only remote that `enable` now refuses. Moving the rule into `strategy` would flip existing repos to fail-closed, so it belongs on its own.

**Smaller items, one line each:**

- `validateCheckpointPushRemote`: the `gitremote.GetRemoteURLInDir` call is `git remote get-url`, i.e. exactly the check that cannot detect a pushurl-only remote, so it can only fail when the following `git config --get remote.<name>.url` also fails — and on the flag path `pushURLsByRemote` has already established existence. Two subprocesses where one does the work.
- "cannot be combined" is checked twice, in `prepareEnableCheckpointRemoteCommand` and again in `prepareEnableCheckpointRemote`; the second is unreachable through the picker path, which returns early on `opts.CheckpointRemote != ""`.
- `prepareEnableCheckpointRemote` calls `settings.Load` before its `if !explicit { return choice, nil }`, so the load is discarded on the common path.
- The picker description says `Detected %d Git remotes` from `len(topology.destinations)`, which counts pinned and ineligible remotes — the number can exceed the choices actually shown.
- `report` is ~90 lines across eight output branches and calls `inspectRemoteTopology` twice; the destination-resolution half and the fanout/hint half would read better split.
- `REDACTED` returns `defaultMirrorRemote` from the stub picker where it means `"origin"`; borrowing a mirror-command constant makes the assertion harder to read than it needs to be.
- `gitRunner` is `repo_mirror_use.go`s package-level test seam; reusing it here couples enable to the mirror tests.
- The README addition is hard-wrapped at ~80 columns while the paragraphs immediately above and below it are one line each, and the two doc blocks largely restate one another in passive voice ("Valid explicit selections and effective dedicated checkpoint repositories are preserved").
